hints: In $\triangle PCQ$, sides are $CP = CQ = 4\text{ cm}$ and $PQ = 4\text{ cm}$, making $\triangle PCQ$ an equilateral triangle.
Use $\angle PCQ = \frac{\pi}{3}\text{ rad}$ to show $\angle PCS = \pi - \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{2\pi}{3}\text{ rad}$.
walkthrough:
Consider triangle $\triangle PCQ$ formed by the radius lines $CP = 4\text{ cm}, CQ = 4\text{ cm}$ and chord $PQ = 4\text{ cm}$:
Since all three sides are equal, $\triangle PCQ$ is equilateral, giving:
$$\angle PCQ = \frac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$$

By symmetry along the line of centers, the angle $\angle PCS$ is supplementary:
$$\angle PCS = \pi - \angle PCQ = \pi - \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{2\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$$

ai_rubric.Circular Measure: Identifies equilateral $\triangle PCQ$ or uses trigonometry $\sin(\angle HCP) = 2/4$ (M1). Shows $\angle PCS = \frac{2\pi}{3}$ clearly (A1).

hints: Calculate the length of the two circular arcs $PS$ and $QR$ with radius $4$ and angle $\frac{2\pi}{3}$.
Calculate the perimeter of the two semicircular boundaries with diameter $4$ (radius $2$).
Sum all boundary components to find the exact perimeter.
walkthrough:
Calculate the total arc length of the two outer circular arcs $PS$ and $QR$ (each with radius $R = 4\text{ cm}$ and angle $\theta = \frac{2\pi}{3}$):
$$\text{Arc } PS + \text{Arc } QR = 2 \times (R\theta) = 2 \times \left(4 \times \frac{2\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{16\pi}{3}\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the circumference contribution from the two semicircles of radius $r = 2\text{ cm}$:
$$\text{Two semicircles} = 2 \times (\pi r) = 2 \times (2\pi) = 4\pi = \frac{12\pi}{3}\text{ cm}$$

Sum both components to obtain the exact perimeter of the metal plate:
$$\text{Perimeter} = \frac{16\pi}{3} + \frac{12\pi}{3} = \frac{28\pi}{3}\text{ cm}$$

ai_rubric.Circular Measure: Calculates two arcs as $\frac{16\pi}{3}$ (M1). Adds semicircles circumference $4\pi$ (M1). States exact perimeter $\frac{28\pi}{3}\text{ cm}$ (A1).

skill_tags: Finding Areas of Composite Circular Regions

hints: Calculate the area of the large circular disc $\pi(4^2) = 16\pi$.
Calculate the area of segment $PQ = \text{Area}(\text{sector } CPQ) - \text{Area}(\triangle CPQ) = \frac{8\pi}{3} - 4\sqrt{3}$.
Calculate the area of one removed semicircle of radius $2$: $\frac{1}{2}\pi(2^2) = 2\pi$.
Subtract two segments and two semicircles from the whole disc.
walkthrough:
Calculate the total area of the original circular disc with radius $R = 4\text{ cm}$:
$$\text{Area}(\text{disc}) = \pi R^2 = \pi(4^2) = 16\pi\text{ cm}^2$$

Calculate the area of sector $CPQ$ and the equilateral triangle $\triangle CPQ$:
$$\text{Area}(\text{sector } CPQ) = \frac{1}{2}(4^2)\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{8\pi}{3}\text{ cm}^2$$
$$\text{Area}(\triangle CPQ) = \frac{1}{2}(4^2)\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = 8\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 4\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$$

Find the area of the segment beyond chord $PQ$ and the area of the removed semicircle:
$$\text{Area}(\text{segment } PQ) = \frac{8\pi}{3} - 4\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$$
$$\text{Area}(\text{semicircle}) = \frac{1}{2}\pi(2^2) = 2\pi\text{ cm}^2$$

Subtract both pairs of removed shapes from the circular disc to find the plate area:
$$\text{Area}(\text{plate}) = 16\pi - 2(2\pi) - 2\left(\frac{8\pi}{3} - 4\sqrt{3}\right) = 12\pi - \frac{16\pi}{3} + 8\sqrt{3} = \left(\frac{20\pi}{3} + 8\sqrt{3}\right)\text{ cm}^2$$

ai_rubric.Area of Circular Shapes: Calculates sector $CPQ = \frac{8\pi}{3}$ (M1). Calculates segment area $\frac{8\pi}{3} - 4\sqrt{3}$ (M1). Calculates semicircle area $2\pi$ (M1). Subtracts from whole disc $16\pi$ (M1). Shows area is $\left(\frac{20\pi}{3} + 8\sqrt{3}\right)\text{ cm}^2$ (A1).
